ideas.description: Replace the template recipe in submissions/arena/ with an airbench96-style net. Layers: frozen 2x2 patch-whitening conv (eigendecomposition computed in prepare), then three blocks of 3 convs with widths 128/384/576, BN, GELU, maxpool, then a scaled linear head with 100 outputs. Use dirac init on block convs. Train with Nesterov SGD using airbench96 lr, wd and momentum, label smoothing 0.2, Lookahead, and a linear warmup/decay schedule. Hold the full uint8 dataset on the GPU and do flip (alternating), translate 4 and cutout 12 on the GPU. Batch 1024, 8.5 epochs, bf16, channels_last, no TTA. torch.compile and warmup run in build on synthetic data; eval uses a separate path that is legal for any B. Run it twice in a row to measure the noise floor.
ideas.expected: Feasible on the first try: accuracy ~0.752-0.758 and time ~7-9 s. Between the two repeats, accuracy spread <= 0.3 pp and time spread <= 0.2 s. If accuracy is < 0.753, the next epoch idea sets feasibility.

ideas.description: On the H1.1.1 recipe, change only the epoch count to 10 (schedule rescaled to match). This secures a feasible anchor and gives one point for the accuracy-vs-epoch slope.
ideas.expected: Accuracy rises ~0.6-1.2 pp over 8.5 epochs, to ~0.762-0.768. Time rises roughly linearly, ~+1.3-1.6 s over the 8.5-epoch run. The slope and intercept tell us where the 0.753 crossing is.

ideas.description: On the H1.1.1 recipe, change only the epoch count to 7 (schedule rescaled). This is the lower point of the sweep, used to interpolate the cheapest feasible epoch count.
ideas.expected: Accuracy drops ~0.8-1.5 pp below 8.5 epochs, to ~0.740-0.747 (infeasible). Time is ~1.2 s lower. A smooth monotone curve confirms H1.1.2; a sharp cliff refutes the smooth-interpolation part.

ideas.description: On the best feasible airbench96 recipe, change only the compile setting: default compile becomes torch.compile(mode='max-autotune'), with CUDA-graph capture of the fixed-shape train step done in build. Handle the last partial batch by dropping it or padding it to a fixed shape. Eval stays on a separate non-graphed dynamic path; check B in {1, 7, 1024} under 5 s.
ideas.expected: Time falls 5-12% (~0.4-1.0 s) and accuracy changes by < 0.3 pp. If the gain is under 3%, launch overhead is not the bottleneck.

ideas.description: At the 8.5-epoch airbench96 recipe, change only the regularization: remove cutout and lower label smoothing from 0.2 to 0.1. Translate and flip stay as they are.
ideas.expected: In the under-fitting regime, accuracy rises +0.3-0.8 pp at equal time. If the gain is >= 0.4 pp, an ~0.5-epoch cut becomes possible later. If accuracy falls, the airbench96 defaults are already well regularized for 100 classes.

ideas.description: At the 8.5-epoch airbench96 recipe (which uses alternating flip), change only the flip to standard random per-image flip. This is the reverse ablation, testing whether alternating flip contributes on CIFAR-100.
ideas.expected: Random flip lowers 3-seed accuracy by ~0.2-0.5 pp at the same time. A drop >= 0.3 pp supports H4.3.1; a drop within noise (< 0.2 pp) refutes it for this budget.

ideas.description: On the best feasible recipe, change only the input to the whitening eigendecomposition: compute it on 5,000 randomly chosen training images (patches drawn from them) instead of all 50,000. Everything else stays fixed.
ideas.expected: Time falls ~0.05-0.2 s and accuracy changes by < 0.3 pp. A cheap, nearly free win if prepare is a visible share of the score.

ideas.description: Explore: change only the widths to 128/256/384 (same 3-convs-per-block layout) and set epochs to 10 to compensate for the lower capacity. Compare it with the best feasible 128/384/576 run.
ideas.expected: FLOPs per epoch fall ~45%, but accuracy per epoch drops ~1.5-2.5 pp. Predicted accuracy at 10 epochs is ~0.745-0.755 at a time ~20-30% below the wide net at 8.5 epochs. If it is feasible, that is a large win; if not, it maps the width trade-off.

structured_output.summary:
The queue was empty and only the chance-level baseline (E000) has run. Because of that, I wrote the ideas in dependency order:

- **First (priority 5):** reproduce airbench96 at 128/384/576 widths and 8.5 epochs (H1.1.1). It runs twice to set the noise floor and should give the first feasible run, around 8 s.
- **Epoch sweep (H1.1.2):** a 10-epoch run (priority 4) secures a feasible fallback, and a 7-epoch run (priority 3) gives the lower point for interpolating the crossing at 0.753.
- **Exploit ideas on that recipe:**
  - max-autotune plus CUDA graphs (H2.2.1).
  - Weaker regularization, removing cutout and lowering label smoothing to 0.1 (H4.1.1). If it helps, it allows fewer epochs.
  - Whitening computed on 5,000 images (H2.3.1), a cheap cut to prepare time.
- **Explore ideas:**
  - Swap alternating flip for random flip to test whether alternating flip helps on CIFAR-100 (H4.3.1).
  - A narrower 128/256/384 net at 10 epochs (H1.2.1).

I left the Muon, proxy-filtering and progressive-resizing ideas for later. They only make sense once there is a tuned feasible baseline to compare against.
